title: The host, with text
caption: The new AppKit host painting through the Metal renderer: Core Text glyphs from an atlas, a caret, a focused field, a checkbox and a list. Typing goes through the Mac's text-input path, and every control in the accessibility tree is named by its claim id (^1 field, ^2 checkbox, ^3 Add, ^4#1 the new item). This app is the host's test fixture, with its frames built in Swift; the next video is the same host running a Lean app.

title: Boundary spike
caption: The first thing on screen. Lean owns the state, the layout and the hit test; Swift forwards clicks and paints Lean's rectangles with Metal. The bar is the count (no text rendering yet). Reset (red) exists only while the count is above zero, which is proved in Lean, and here it's pressed through the accessibility tree.
